Early in his first term, under mounting scrutiny over his relationship with
Russia, Donald Trump
[demanded](https://www.nytimes.com/2018/01/04/us/politics/trump-sessions-
russia-mcgahn.html) of underlings: "Where's my Roy Cohn?"

He was referring to the amoral political pit bull who tutored him as a young
real estate developer. Cohn, who became famous as the odious sidekick to anti-
communist demagogue Joe McCarthy in the 1950s, stood for ferocious pursuit of
self-interest and attacks on anyone standing in the way.

The bottom line he imparted: Right and wrong have nothing to do with it.

Cohn's philosophy has defined Trump's 10-year reign over American politics.
And it helps explain the colossal scandal involving his administration, chip-
maker Nvidia's disgraced CEO Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy.
